content:
Yesterday we heard the voice of Caleb quieting the people, and we saw how dangerous a bad report can be among the flock. We ended by noticing that even while the ten spies were spreading fear with their mouths, they were still carrying the proof of Yahweh's faithfulness in their arms. Today we look at those fruits, for they were not meaningless. They were samples of the promise, and each one has something to teach us.

First, they brought grapes. Grapes in the Bible are connected with vineyards, wine, joy, blessing, and fruitfulness. Psalm 104:15 says God gives wine to make the heart glad. God often speaks of Israel as His vineyard, for Isaiah 5:7 says, "The nation of Israel is the vineyard of the LORD of Heaven's Armies." And our Master said, "Yes, I am the vine; you are the branches" (John 15:5). The great cluster of grapes from Eshcol showed that Canaan was not empty. It was rich with fruit. Spiritually, the grapes remind us of the joy, the blessing, and the fruitfulness that Yahweh has promised to His people. The promised inheritance is not barren. It is not dry. It is full of life and joy. And the cluster itself gives us another beautiful picture, for many grapes were joined together in one single cluster. In the same way, many members are joined together in one body under Christ. Paul says, "The human body has many parts, but the many parts make up one whole body. So it is with the body of Christ" (1 Corinthians 12:12). One grape alone is small, but a cluster carried by two men was a visible testimony of abundance. Yahweh is not preparing isolated fruits. He is preparing a united body. The New Creation is called to abide in Christ, the true vine, and to bear fruit together for Yahweh's glory, for our Master said, "Those who remain in me, and I in them, will produce much fruit" (John 15:5).

Second, the spies brought figs. The fig tree is often connected with peace, security, settled blessing, and the spiritual condition of Yahweh's people. In the days of Solomon, the kingdom enjoyed peace and prosperity, and 1 Kings 4:25 says, "Throughout the lifetime of Solomon, all of Judah and Israel lived in peace and safety. Each family had its own home and garden." The older wording says that every man lived under his vine and under his fig tree. That phrase speaks of peace, rest, safety, and settled blessing. No fear. No wandering. No slavery. No war disturbing every house. Each one dwelling securely under his own vine and fig tree. And this shows us something in the promise given to us also. Yahweh has promised rest; not the restless life of this present evil world, but true peace under the reign of Christ. Hebrews 4:9 says, "So there is a special rest still waiting for the people of God." The fig also reminds us of our spiritual condition, for a fruitful fig tree shows blessing, while a barren fig tree warns of failure. Our Master once looked for fruit on a fig tree and found none, for Mark 11:13 says, "But there were only leaves." The lesson is that Yahweh looks for true fruit, and not for leaves only. So the figs of the land speak of peace and settled blessing, but also of the fruitful condition Yahweh desires to find in His people.

Third, the spies brought pomegranates. Pomegranates are connected with beauty, fullness, holiness, and priestly fruitfulness. On the robe of the high priest, pomegranates were placed along the hem. Exodus 28:33-34 says, "Make pomegranates out of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and attach them to the hem of the robe, with gold bells between them. The gold bells and pomegranates are to alternate all around the hem." Pomegranates were also used in the decoration of Solomon's temple, for 1 Kings 7:20 speaks of the pomegranates arranged around the tops of the pillars. Now a pomegranate is full of many seeds, and so it carries the thought of fullness and abundant life. And because it was used on priestly garments and on temple pillars, it also carries the thought of holy beauty before Yahweh. This speaks beautifully of the promise set before the New Creation, for Yahweh is preparing a priestly company; beautiful in holiness, full of life, and set apart for His service. Peter says, "And you are living stones that God is building into his spiritual temple. What's more, you are his holy priests" (1 Peter 2:5). And again he says, "You are royal priests, a holy nation, God's very own possession" (1 Peter 2:9).

So the fruits of the land speak powerfully to us. The grapes show joy, blessing, and fruitfulness in the vine. The figs show peace, rest, and settled blessing. The pomegranates show holiness, beauty, fullness, and priestly service. These were not empty fruits. They were samples of the promise. They were proofs placed before all Israel. Yahweh allowed the spies to bring back the evidence of the land before the whole congregation, so that the people did not have to imagine whether the land was good. They could see it with their own eyes and hold it in their own hands. And in the same way, Yahweh has given us samples of the coming inheritance. We have not yet entered immortality, but we have tasted the powers of the age to come through His Word. We have not yet sat upon the throne, but we have received the promise. We have not yet seen the Kingdom fill the earth, but prophecy has shown it to us beforehand. We have not yet entered the full rest, but the Spirit of Yahweh gives us a foretaste of what is coming. Hebrews 6:4-5 speaks of those who have "tasted the goodness of the word of God and the power of the age to come." The Word gives us the fruit of the land before we enter the land. Prophecy gives us a cluster from Eshcol. The promises give us figs and pomegranates before the inheritance is fully possessed. And the resurrection of Christ itself is the firstfruits, proving that the rest of the harvest will surely come, for Paul says, "But in fact, Christ has been raised from the dead. He is the first of a great harvest of all who have died" (1 Corinthians 15:20).

Therefore we have no reason to fear. Yahweh has already shown us more than enough fruit to trust Him. He has shown us the resurrection of Christ. He has shown us the promise of immortality. He has shown us the coming throne.

He has shown us the rest that remains. He has shown us the Kingdom that will one day fill the earth. And yet, even after all these precious promises, it is still possible to fall away through unbelief. Israel saw the fruit, heard the promise, and stood at the very border; yet they turned back in their hearts. Their example is written as a warning for us. Hebrews 3:19 says, "So we see that because of their unbelief they were not able to enter his rest." And then Hebrews 4:1 warns us, "God's promise of entering his rest still stands, so we ought to tremble with fear that some of you might fail to experience it." This is not a light matter. Israel failed at the border because they did not mix the promise with faith. They heard good news about the land. They saw the fruit. But unbelief made them afraid, and fear made them rebel. Hebrews 4:11 says, "So let us do our best to enter that rest. But if we disobey God, as the people of Israel did, we will fall." This event should pierce our hearts. They fell away and could not enter the rest, and we must not fall away, lest we too fail to enter His rest.

The danger is never that Yahweh's promise will fail. The danger is that fear and unbelief may grow quietly in us. The land was good. The fruit was real. Yahweh was faithful. But the ten spies corrupted the hearts of the people. So we must guard ourselves from that bad-report spirit. When the way becomes difficult, let us not say, "We cannot." Let us say with Caleb, "We can certainly conquer it." When people magnify the giants, let us magnify Yahweh. When people spread panic, let us speak faith. When the flock is troubled, let us become voices like Caleb and Joshua. Let us say, "The road is hard, but Yahweh is faithful. The cross is heavy, but Christ gives strength. The world may hate us, but the Father will keep us. The giants are real, but the promise is greater." Paul said, "If God is for us, who can ever be against us?" (Romans 8:31), and again, "Despite all these things, overwhelming victory is ours through Christ, who loved us" (Romans 8:37).

Therefore let us not stand at the border of the promise and tremble like grasshoppers. The ten spies said, "Next to them we felt like grasshoppers, and that's what they thought, too!" (Numbers 13:33). But faith does not define itself by how small it feels before the enemy. Faith defines the enemy by how small he is before Yahweh. The promised land is before us. The grapes, the figs, and the pomegranates have already been shown to us in the Word. Joy, peace, holiness, priesthood, immortality, the throne, and rest are all promised. Yahweh has not called us to an empty land. He has called us to glory. So let us hold fast, for Hebrews 10:23 says, "Let us hold tightly without wavering to the hope we affirm, for God can be trusted to keep his promise." Let us not be among those who spread fear. Let us not be among those who weaken the flock. Let us not be among those who see the fruit and still speak unbelief. Let us be Calebs. Let us be Joshuas. Let us strengthen the hands of the weak and say, "Yahweh is able. Christ will help us. The promise is true. Let us go up at once." The land is good. The fruit is real. The giants are temporary. The promise is eternal. This brings us to the close of Numbers chapter thirteen, and Yahweh willing, we will step into chapter fourteen tomorrow.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our Father,

We thank You for the promised inheritance You have placed before the New Creation.

Thank You for the hope of immortality, the throne with Christ, and the rest that remains.

Help us not to fear the giants that stand along the narrow way.

Make us like Caleb and Joshua, speaking faith and courage among the flock.

Keep us from unbelief, that we may not fail to enter Your rest as Israel did.

Let the grapes, the figs, and the pomegranates of Your promises strengthen our hearts.

"Now faith is the confidence that what we hope for will actually happen." - Hebrews 11:1

In Christ name we pray. Amen.
